'''''Rhododendron arboreum''''', the '''tree rhododendron''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=17 October 2014 }}</ref> is an [[evergreen]] shrub or small tree with a showy display of bright red flowers. It is found in [[Bhutan]], China, India, [[Myanmar]], [[Nepal]], Sri Lanka, Pakistan and Thailand.<ref>{{Cite web |title=''Rhododendron arboreum'' |url=https://rhododendron.org/blog/?view=plink&id=127 |publisher=[[American Rhododendron Society]] |access-date=20 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250514072239/https://rhododendron.org/blog/?view=plink&id=127 |archive-date=14 May 2025 }}</ref> It is the [[national flower]] of [[Nepal]].

==Description==
Its [[specific epithet]] means "tending to be woody or growing in a tree-like form".{{Citation needed|date=July 2025}} It has been recorded as reaching heights of {{convert|20|m|ft|abbr=on}},<ref>{{cite web |url=http://wildeel.com/rhodotree.html |title=Tree rhododendrons |publisher=Richard Francis |access-date=29 July 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080719144250/http://www.wildeel.com/rhodotree.html <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archive-date=19 July 2008 }}</ref> though it is more usually {{convert|12|m|ft|abbr=on}} tall
and broad. This plant holds the [[Guinness Record]] for the World's Largest Rhododendron. The tree discovered in 1993 at [[Mount Japfü]] in the [[Kohima district|Kohima District]] of [[Nagaland]], India, holds the Guinness Record for the tallest Rhododendron at {{convert|65|ft|m|order=flip|abbr=on}}.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/66509-largest-rhododendron |work=Guinness Book of World Records |title=Largest Rhododendron }}</ref> In sharp contrast to this, the [[New Guinea]]n [[epiphytic]] species ''[[Rhododendron caespitosum]]'' never exceeds {{cvt|10|cm|in|0}} in height.<ref>{{ cite book |last=Sleumer |first=H. |title=[[Flora Malesiana]] – Ericaceae |volume=4 (series 1) |page=571 }}</ref>

In early and mid spring, trusses of 15–20 bell-shaped flowers, {{convert|5|cm|in|round=0.5|abbr=on}} wide and {{convert|3|–|5|cm|in|round=0.5|abbr=on}} long are produced; they are red, pink or white, with black nectar pouches and black spots inside.

===Subspecies===
[[File:Rhododendron arboreum subsp. nilagiricum (1).jpg|thumb|''Rhododendron arboreum'' subsp. ''nilagiricum'', [[Mukurthi National Park]], Tamil Nadu]]
The [[Plants of the World Online]] database accepts five [[subspecies]]:<ref name="POWO">{{Cite web |title=''Rhododendron arboreum'' Sm. |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:331945-1 |access-date=30 September 2025 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en }}</ref>
*''Rhododendron arboreum'' subsp. ''albotomentosum'' <small>(Davidian)</small> D.F.Chamb. has leaves with whitish hairs beneath; it occurs in Myanmar.
*''Rhododendron arboreum'' subsp. ''arboreum'', occurring in the Himalaya.
*''Rhododendron arboreum'' subsp. ''cinnamomeum'' <small>(Wall. ex G.Don)</small> Tagg has leaves with cinnamon-brown hairs beneath; it occurs in the central & eastern Himalaya to southern Tibet.
*''Rhododendron arboreum'' subsp. ''nilagiricum'' <small>(Zenker) Tagg</small> is found in the [[Nilgiri Mountains]] in Tamil Nadu, India.<ref>Chamberlain, D. F. 1982. A revision of Rhododendron II. Subgenus Hymenanthes. Notes Roy. Bot. Gard. Edinburgh 39:331.[https://www.ars-grin.gov/cgi-bin/npgs/html/taxon.pl?418076]</ref>
*''Rhododendron arboreum'' subsp. ''zeylanicum'' <small>(T.J.Booth)</small> Tagg; a rare subspecies endemic in the highlands of Sri Lanka, named after Zeilan, the name used by Arabian traders to refer to Sri Lanka

== Habitat ==
''Rhododendron arboreum'' is found in the Pakistan, India, Nepal, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, the Himalayas, Northeast India, and Tibet. It is introduced in [[Madeira]].<ref name="POWO"/>

It is the [[national flower]] of Nepal.<ref>{{cite book |author=Rohit Kumar |title=Nepal, Nature's Paradise: Insight Into Diverse Facets of Topography, Flora & Ecology  |year=1999 |page=188 |isbn=978-9748614946 }}</ref> In India it is the [[List of Indian state trees|state tree]] of [[Uttarakhand]] and [[List of Indian state flowers|state flower]] of [[Nagaland]]. It is the provincial flower of Sri Lanka's [[Central Province, Sri Lanka|Central Province]].

==Cultivation==
''Rhododendron arboreum'' prefers moist but well-drained, leafy, humus-rich, [[soil pH|acid pH soil]], in dappled shade. It has broad, dark green leaves, {{convert|7|–|19|cm|in|round=0.5|abbr=on}} long, with a silvery, fawn or brown hairy coating beneath.[[File:Fyson179-Rhododendron arboreum.jpg|thumb|''Rhododendron arboreum'' from [[Fyson]]<ref name="FysonII">
{{citation |title=The flora of the Niligiri and Pulney Hill-Tops (Above 6,500 Feet), Being the Wild and Commoner Introduced Flowering Plants Round the Hill-Stations of Kodaikanal, Ootacamund, Kotagiri and Kodaikanal, with 286 full page illustrations and 4 maps |volume=II |page=179 |author=P. F. Fyson |author-link=Philip Furley Fyson |publisher=Superintendent, Government Press |date=1915 |place=Madras }}</ref>]] This plant is suitable for [[woodland garden]]s.

Shelter is imperative to prevent wind damage to leaves.

==Threats==
Rhododendrons are susceptible to vine [[weevil]], rhododendron and azalea [[Whitefly|whiteflies]], [[leafhopper]]s, [[lacebug]]s, scale insects, [[caterpillar]]s, [[aphid]]s, [[powdery mildew]], [[bud blast]], [[honey fungus]], [[Rust (fungus)|rust]], leafy [[gall]], petal [[blight]], [[silver leaf (disease)|silver leaf]], [[Phytophthora cactorum|phytophthora root rot]] and lime-induced [[chlorosis]].<ref>The Royal Horticultural Society (2008) ''RHS Garden Hyde Hall Plant of the month: April'', retrieved 19 February 2008 [http://www.rhs.org.uk/whatson/gardens/hydehall/archive/hydehallpom05apr.asp Gardens] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051120092406/http://www.rhs.org.uk/whatson/gardens/hydehall/archive/hydehallpom05apr.asp |date=20 November 2005 }}</ref>
